subject: Inference costing alignment & pilot gating
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Emma Lawson <emma@clearledger.com>, Tom Blake <tom.blake@clearledger.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2028 15:12:00 -0000
Subject: Inference costing alignment & pilot gating

Hi Emma / Tom — great to meet earlier. Quick post-call summary and concrete next steps so we stay aligned. TL;DR: ClearLedger needs predictable monthly spend below ~$45k and a short pilot that proves 30–50% unit-cost reduction through batching + KV prefix caching; also concerned about peak latency during end-of-day reconciliation jobs.

What we heard (pain & goals):
- Primary pain: unbounded token spend from nightly reconciliation and high-frequency user queries; finance needs a clear upper bound.
- Secondary: tail latencies (95th/99th) during batch reconciles cause timeouts in downstream jobs.
- Goal: 3-week pilot to validate cost controls and prove a reliable path to < $0.025 / 1k tokens equivalent after optimizations (or show where tradeoffs lie).

What Redwood proposes (high level):
- Pilot scope: run ClearLedger's reconciliation and a sampled production traffic slice against a dedicated Redwood pilot environment (dedicated pool) for three weeks.
- Key levers to test: intelligent batching for asynchronous reconciliation, prefix/KV caching for repeated context, and a conservative quantization profile for model-v1-compact.
- Expected outcomes: detailed TCO workbook, unit-cost breakdown by route (reconcile vs user-facing), recommended batching config + expected savings range (30–50% typical), and a rollout checklist for production.

Constraints & asks from ClearLedger we captured:
- Monthly budget cap target: ~$45k (stated by Tom).
- Security: need SOC2 evidence and basic network allowlist during pilot.
- Success criteria: unit-cost delta and latency SLO maintained at 95th percentile < 400ms for user routes; reconciliation job completion time reduced by >= 20%.

Immediate next steps (owners & timeline):
1) Redwood (Marissa / Karthik) -> deliver initial TCO workbook + pilot pricing estimate by Tue 3/19. (attachment: redwood-tco-estimate.xlsx)
2) ClearLedger (Emma) -> confirm the two sample reconciliation jobs and provide sample logs + a short traffic CSV by Mon 3/19.
3) All -> 30-min follow-up to finalize SOW and allowlist window on Wed 3/20. I'll send a calendar invite.

Questions we still have:
- Emma: which reconciliation job is highest priority if we need to limit scope?
- Tom: is the $45k cap a hard procurement ceiling or a target we can stretch with demonstrated ROI?

Attachments: redwood-tco-estimate.xlsx (draft) — see key assumptions tab for token model and latency buckets.

Thanks — looking forward to getting the pilot running quickly.

Lauren Bishop
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
lauren@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Emma Lawson <emma@clearledger.com>

Date: Sat, 16 Mar 2028 01:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inference costing alignment & pilot gating

Thanks Lauren — helpful summary and appreciated the clarity. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Priority job: 'end_of_day_reconcile' is the one causing the most token churn and the nightly spike; start there.
- Budget: $45k is our procurement target; procurement can stretch to ~$55k with an executive sign-off if we can show payback within 3 months.
- Security: we can share the SOC2 cert and we'll need to add Redwood's pilot IPs to our allowlist; Marissa / Karthik, I can open a ticket with our security team once you share the IP range.

We can turn around the sample logs by EOD Mon (3/19). Please proceed with the TCO workbook and a short, line-item SOW so procurement has something to review.

Emma

- Include a conservative quantization option and call out any quality-risk indicators.
